## Data

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# setup
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# drop rows missing flipper length or species
penguins = load_penguins().dropna(subset=["flipper_length_mm", "species"])
```

The Palmer Penguins dataset records measurements from 344 penguins across three species (Adelie, Chinstrap, Gentoo) sampled at Palmer Station, Antarctica. This post looks at one measurement: flipper length.

## Summary

```{python}
#| label: tbl-flipper-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary statistics of flipper length (mm) across penguin species."
# summary
summary = (
    penguins
    .groupby("species")["flipper_length_mm"]
    .agg(["mean", "median", "std", "min", "max", "count"])
    .round(1)
)
summary
```

Based on flipper length, the three species differ noticeably. Adelie penguins have the shortest flippers on average, Chinstraps sit in the middle, and Gentoos are clearly the largest.

## Visualization


```{python}
#| label: fig-flipper-boxplot
#| fig-cap: "Flipper length distribution by penguin species. Gentoo penguins have the longest flippers by a wide margin."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4.5))
species_order = ["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"]
data = [penguins.loc[penguins["species"] == s, "flipper_length_mm"] for s in species_order]

ax.boxplot(data, label=species_order, patch_artist=True)
ax.set_ylabel("Flipper length (mm)")
ax.set_xlabel("Species")
ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.3)
plt.show()
```

## Inference

From the figure, it's evident that the gap between Gentoo and the other two species is large enough that flipper length alone would be a decent classifier for that species particularly. Adelie and Chinstrap overlap considerably in flipper length, so distinguishing between those two would need additional features than flipper length.
